implementations.summary: Money as an integer count of minor units — add/subtract/scale/allocate with explicit rounding, and a currency that is checked rather than assumed. Float currency is a defect class, not a style choice.

implementations.name: financeTxn
implementations.summary: The shared transaction shape every finance capability folds over, plus the merchant key that makes recurrence detectable — a charge rarely writes itself identically twice.

tests.name: financeTxn

implementations.name: recurring
implementations.summary: Find standing charges from transaction history and report what each costs a YEAR — the number that prompts a cancellation, where the monthly figure prompts nothing. Scores regularity and amount stability separately so a utility whose amount moves is still detected.

tests.name: recurring

implementations.name: duplicates
implementations.summary: Charges that may be the same charge twice, SCORED rather than pronounced — built from how improbable the coincidence is and damped by how habitual the merchant is, because the false positive is what kills the feature.

tests.name: duplicates

implementations.name: fees
implementations.summary: Every fee and interest charge gathered into one place with what can be done about each — and a repeating fee flagged as a standing condition, where one change stops the whole stream.

tests.name: fees

implementations.name: income
implementations.summary: What arrives and how much it MOVES — median and spread per source, not a mean. Two people averaging the same have different situations if one is salaried and the other invoices lumpily, and every downstream question turns on the low months.

tests.name: income

implementations.name: projection
implementations.summary: Income projected forward as a BAND that widens with distance, with every assumption written down — and a refusal, rather than a band of zeroes, when the history is too thin to mean anything. A lapsed source is dropped and named.

tests.name: projection

implementations.name: reconcile
implementations.summary: The gate every derived figure passes through. Arithmetic over an INCOMPLETE transaction list produces a plausible number rather than an error, so reconciliation is a TYPE: only a passing reconcile can mint a ReconciledLedger, and coverage is the LEAST covered account. No tolerance — money is integers, so a one-cent gap is a real row missing, doubled or mis-signed.

tests.name: reconcile

implementations.name: position
implementations.summary: What is actually held and actually owed, as of a date coverage really reaches — the first capability that TAKES a ReconciledLedger. The sign contract is the whole module: a card statement prints what you OWE, so adding it to a chequing balance produces a quantity that does not exist. The proof is that a payment from chequing to a card moves nothing.

tests.name: position

implementations.name: obligations
implementations.summary: What is due, on what day, between now and the horizon. Stepping is the whole problem: a monthly charge is NOT every 30 days, so calendar cadences step by calendar months and CLAMP into short months instead of rolling into the next one — and the anchor never moves, so a bill on the 31st does not walk backwards through the year.

tests.name: obligations

implementations.name: runway
implementations.summary: How long the money lasts, reported on the LOW income band — a runway on expected income is right on average and useless in the case that matters. Discretionary spending is a REQUIRED argument and the horizon TRUNCATES at the obligation calendar, because both would otherwise read as zero and lengthen the runway on missing data.

tests.name: runway

implementations.name: spending
implementations.summary: Where the money actually goes, and the one thing it exists to get right: A TRANSFER IS NOT SPENDING. Paying a card from chequing looks like an outflow but is the same money in a different place, and the calendar already carries the minimum — counting it here subtracts it from the runway twice. Categorisation is a deterministic local table, and what it cannot place is UNCATEGORISED rather than 'other'.

tests.name: spending

implementations.name: viable
implementations.summary: The smallest monthly income that holds, as a LADDER — survival / current / stable / progress — measured on the WORST month, not the average. An annual renewal makes one month cost $900 more than the other eleven, and an income covering the median clears every month except the one it does not.

tests.name: viable

implementations.name: priority
implementations.summary: Where THIS month's spare money goes. Minimums first; then a BUFFER, which beats the rate until it exists, because paying a card to zero and then meeting a repair puts the repair back on the card WITH a fee; then the rate — except a 0% promotion, which is worthless to pay while it runs and the most urgent thing on the list when it is about to end.

tests.name: priority

implementations.name: ingest
implementations.summary: What a bank actually exports, turned into the shapes everything else runs on. Four things that look like parsing and are not: the SIGN (Discover writes a purchase positive, Bank of America writes it negative), the DATE (03/04 is two dates and an all-under-13 file is genuinely ambiguous), the AMOUNT (a float multiply loses a cent before anything can check itself), and the COMMAS. Every packaged profile is UNVERIFIED and says so.

tests.name: ingest

implementations.name: transfer
implementations.summary: Prices a balance transfer honestly, starting from the sentence the marketing never contains: a balance transfer DOES NOT REDUCE DEBT. It moves it and charges for the move, so the instant it completes you owe the balance plus the fee. Everything good about it is a bet that the interest avoided beats the fee, and this names every way that bet is lost.

tests.name: transfer

implementations.name: negotiate
implementations.summary: The case for the phone call, assembled from your own data. THE ASK DEPENDS ON WHETHER YOU CAN PAY: a rate reduction when the runway holds, a hardship plan when it does not — and that call must come BEFORE a missed payment, because after it the delinquency is already reported and no arrangement takes it back. Evidence is only ever what the data supports.

tests.name: negotiate

implementations.name: connection
implementations.summary: The credential model and the policy that decides what to try next against an institution. A bug here does not produce a wrong number, it produces a FROZEN ACCOUNT — so an auth failure is NEVER retried, a transport failure is, MFA is a handoff rather than an obstacle, a fresh session is the lockout-avoidance mechanism, and the manual file-drop path is always available and always last.

tests.name: connection

implementations.name: bsc-fin--session
implementations.summary: Stored sessions, and the one question the Rust side asks: may an unattended fetch happen right now. The driver NEVER types a credential — a person signs in, the session is stored, everything automated only reuses one. Deliberately NARROWER than the TypeScript policy and conservative against it: it may answer Go only where that one would say use-session.

implementations.name: bsc-fin--inbox
implementations.summary: Where statement exports land, and the rule that stops one being counted twice. Reading the same file again does not error — it doubles a month of spending and every number stays plausible — so a file is CLAIMED once read, moved out of the inbox, and a claim never overwrites. A name whose institution cannot be read is refused rather than guessed, because the wrong profile reads a date as an amount and says so confidently.

implementations.name: useGlanceProjects

tests.name: useGlanceProjects — declared role/health/activity (#2284/#2541)

implementations.name: opportunity
implementations.summary: Public funding — grants, SBIR, federal and state contracts — reduced to ONE comparable number: expected value per hour of bid effort, against what billing the same hours would pay. Refuses rather than discounts: what you cannot legally win is not ranked, a deadline you cannot make is a no rather than a lower-confidence yes, and an unknown hit rate is undefined rather than a default somebody would act on.

tests.name: opportunity

implementations.name: series
implementations.summary: reconcile for market data: nothing derived from a price series until it is checked. Every way a series lies is a way a strategy looks profitable — look-ahead above all, which barsAvailableAt answers structurally by handing back only bars STRICTLY before the decision date. Survivorship and adjustment are DECLARED, never inferred, and a universe claim on an undeclared series is refused.

tests.name: series

implementations.name: brief
implementations.summary: Every capability in the feature folded into ONE ranked list of what to do. It COMPOSES and never recomputes — a second implementation of a number is a second answer. Two tiers because one ordering cannot hold both: dated work sorted by WHEN, everything else by worth PER HOUR OF EFFORT. Absent is not zero — a capability that never ran is NAMED, because a brief reporting nothing available when nothing looked is the lie that makes somebody stop looking.

tests.name: brief

implementations.name: bsc-fin--account
implementations.summary: The account registry, and more usefully what it CANNOT tell you. position needs to know what an account IS before a balance means anything, and none of that is in a statement export. Every gap names the capability it silently blocks — an agent's next question after a missing number is always why, and without an answer it invents one. An account NUMBER is refused at any depth.

implementations.name: bsc-fin--txn
implementations.summary: The shared transaction shape, ported from TypeScript. One definition, so the crate does not carry six subtly different ideas of what a transaction is. merchantKey SPLITS FIRST then drops any token carrying a digit — stripping digits first leaves the letter fragments of an order id behind, so one merchant keys differently on every occurrence and matches itself never.

implementations.name: bsc-fin--reconcile
implementations.summary: The gate every derived figure passes through, ported from TypeScript. Arithmetic over an INCOMPLETE transaction list produces a plausible number rather than an error, so reconciliation is a TYPE — and the Rust brand is STRONGER than the TypeScript one: private fields make external construction a compile error with no cast to defeat it.

implementations.name: bsc-fin--position
implementations.summary: What is held and what is owed, as of a date coverage really reaches — the first capability that TAKES a ReconciledLedger. Reads the account REGISTRY directly rather than a parallel declaration type, so bsc fin account feeds it. The sign contract is the whole module: a card statement prints what you OWE, so adding it to a chequing balance produces a quantity that does not exist.

implementations.name: bsc-fin--balance
implementations.summary: Balances, and the conversion that happens at the boundary rather than in somebody's head. A person types what the statement PRINTS — a card says 2431.07 and means you owe it — so the store takes the printed figure and the account's kind and converts. Without the kind the sign is unknowable, so a balance for an undeclared account is refused rather than stored unconverted.
